# mirrorslope 0.2.1

CRAN preparation.

* The difference label is now drawn with plotmath (`Delta ~ "= +4.2%"`) and an
  ASCII minus sign, so it renders on every graphics device including the `pdf()`
  device used by `R CMD check`. Previously the literal U+0394 and U+2212 glyphs
  failed with "conversion failure ... mbcsToSbcs" on devices with single-byte
  encodings.
* Multi-line `@importFrom` tags joined; `NAMESPACE` is now generated by roxygen2.
* `dplyr`, `grid` and `magrittr` removed from Imports (never used).
* `.Rbuildignore` added; developer notes no longer ship in the tarball.

# mirrorslope 0.2.0

Publication-quality rendering refinements.

## New features

* `mirror_slope_plot()` gains `y_percent` (default `TRUE`) to format y-axis
  ticks and header statistics with a percent sign; set `FALSE` for
  absolute-scale outcomes.
* `mirror_slope_plot()` gains `jitter_points` (default `FALSE`) to spread
  overlapping individual endpoints horizontally for readability, reproducible
  via `seed`.

## Improvements

* Directional "to <endpoint>" arrows now flow inward toward the centre on both
  arms, reinforcing that the horizontal axis is positional and not a time axis.
* The baseline reference line at zero is now a clearer dashed line, and a dashed
  vertical guide marks the central convergence axis.
* Footnotes with embedded line breaks render as multiple left-aligned lines.
* Header statistics show a percent sign when `y_percent = TRUE`.
* The between-group annotation is now drawn as a bracket sized to the treatment gap (with end serifs), rather than a rule sized to the text block, so the bracket measures the difference it labels.

## Journal-quality refinements

* Individual trajectory lines are now drawn from each subject's baseline to the
  central endpoint only, grouped by arm and subject, so no line crosses the
  centre or connects across arms. This removes the main source of visual clutter.
* Mean-endpoint diamonds now sit on a small white halo so they read cleanly
  where the converging lines crowd the central knot.
* Directional arrows are lighter and smaller, receding as chart furniture.

* The difference bracket is now a thin hairline matching the axis weight, with
  short inward serifs and more space before the annotation text, for a cleaner
  measurement mark.
* Chart furniture (axis lines, ticks, gridlines, reference lines, arrows) now
  uses a single coherent light hairline family so nothing competes with the data.
* Slope echoes are shorter and more muted, reading as a subtle continuation hint
  rather than data.
* `theme_mirror()` now sets a clean sans typeface, a clear title/subtitle/caption
  hierarchy, and refined spacing; `base_family` defaults to a Helvetica/Arial/sans
  stack and can be overridden.
* Default mean-line width and marker size were reduced slightly for print.
* `save_path` documents vector output (.pdf/.svg) for journal submission.

# mirrorslope 0.1.0

Initial release.

## Features

* `prep_mirror_data()` prepares a long analysis dataset into a `mirror_data`
  object: validates structure, applies population flags with AND logic, retains
  baseline and endpoint visits, assigns role columns, counts analysed N per arm,
  and records provenance metadata (schema version, filters, timestamp, call).
* `add_summary()` attaches group-level estimates and the baseline each mean line
  is drawn from, supporting both change-from-baseline (baseline 0) and
  absolute-scale outcomes.
* `add_precision()` attaches per-arm standard errors or confidence intervals.
* `add_difference()` attaches the between-arm difference with optional standard
  error, confidence interval, and p-value; warns on sign inconsistency.
* `mirror_slope_plot()` renders the figure as a standard `ggplot` object.
  Optional elements (individual trajectories, difference band, relative-benefit
  annotation, per-arm precision, N in the strip header) are off by default and
  shown only on request. The annotation zone auto-expands the x-axis without
  altering the data panel.
* `mirror_palette()` provides `"default"`, `"colorblind"` (Okabe-Ito), and
  `"capricor"` palettes.
* `theme_mirror()` supplies a publication theme with proportional text scaling.
* S3 methods `print()`, `summary()`, and `as.data.frame()` for `mirror_data`.

## Design notes

* The `mirror_data` structure conforms to a versioned specification (schema 1.0)
  shared with a companion SAS macro, so both tools produce equivalent figures
  from equivalent inputs.
* `direction` describes the direction of numeric movement (endpoint versus
  baseline). For outcomes where the favourable direction is unusual, supply
  `outcome_label` and `benefit_label` explicitly.

## Known limitations

* Right-to-left and non-Latin arm labels in strip headers are not yet supported.
* Multi-endpoint layouts are produced by combining plots with an external layout
  package such as **patchwork** rather than within `mirrorslope`.
